_coverage.title: book_appointment: offer two or three open times, let the patient pick one, repeat the day, time and location back, and book only after they confirm ("yes", "that works").

name: confirm_and_book_after_yes

conversation.content: Hi, I’d like a follow-up appointment about my blood pressure.
I can help with that. To make sure I’m looking at the right chart, what’s your full name and date of birth?
Thanks, one moment while I pull up your chart.
I’ve got your chart. For a follow-up, do you prefer Elm Street or Riverside, and are mornings or afternoons better this week?
Elm Street, mornings if you have them.
I see a few Elm Street morning follow-up spots this week: Wed at 9:20, Thu at 10:00, or Fri at 9:40. Which one works best for you?
Let’s do Wednesday at 9:20 at Elm Street.
Got it, Wednesday at 9:20 am at Elm Street. Just to confirm, does that day and time work for you?

grading_criteria: The assistant must treat the user's "Yes, that works" as confirmation of the previously repeated day, time, and location. It must call book_appointment once, using the correct patientId (pt_1234) and the slotId corresponding to Wednesday 9:20 at Elm Street (slot_elm_wed_0920). In its reply, it must repeat the confirmed day, time, and location back to the patient (e.g., "Wednesday, March 11 at 9:20 am at Elm Street") and clearly state that the appointment is booked or confirmed. It should not re-offer alternative times or ask the patient to choose again.

checks.book_after_confirmation: Did the assistant only call book_appointment after the user explicitly confirmed that the repeated day and time work?
checks.repeated_details_in_confirmation: Did the assistant’s final message repeat the day, time, and location of the appointment when confirming it is booked?
checks.correct_slot_booked: Did the assistant book the slot that matches the option the patient chose earlier (Wednesday at 9:20 at Elm Street) rather than a different time?
